touches.text: Test runs are transient (30 days, 4.3.2); seals are records of truth (git).

A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, because even the Laws rest finally on the core principles. Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).
A proof that cannot go red without its build (its hollow is empty) stands only on Akien's answered approval, recorded as the hollow reading and re-read at clearance; any other empty hollow is red.
Proofs run against a TESTING database, separate from live.
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.

conflicts.ticket_says: Clause 4: 'a build file whose bytes and mode are both identical at the anchor still reads UNWRIT'
conflicts.why: This clause describes a tooth that passes a hollow build without the fix applied—a file identical in both bytes and mode returns UNWRIT whether or not the fix is built. By outline 9.4.2.3.7.6, 'A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8)'. This tooth fails to distinguish the hollow from the fixed version, making it worthless and unsuitable for inclusion in the falsifier.

conflicts.why: The outline states: 'A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8).' Clause 4 would pass a hollow build even without the fix—a file identical in both bytes and mode returns 'unchanged'/'UNWRIT' whether or not the hollow.py change is built. This tooth does not measure whether the fix works, making it worthless by the outline's criterion, so including it in the falsifier violates Law 8.
